body:
Oh, I noticed a similar thing when I was using my linux machine the other day. But, like you, I thought it was a drivers + gnome3 issue.

Any chance you could figure out since which version that is happening?

You can download previous version of the library using this link format:

https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/archive/r65.zip
https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/archive/r64.zip
https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/archive/r63.zip
...
Yes, I'll find a version that introduced this behavior and update the bug report.
Thanks!
Version r64 works OK, so it is some recent change. I'll try finding a commit with 'git bisect'.
Oh, that'd be super helpful :+1:

This change introduced the problem: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/commit/04ce05d49c9f8d2c4f29bbb824ffd60a6ceb415c
Let me know if I can help with debugging, but maybe the culprit will be immediately obvious to someone familiar with that code.

@wrr  Physically-based shading used to be an option. It is now always implemented.
Can you run r.64 with renderer.physicallyBasedShading = true?
@WestLangley you are right, r.64 with renderer.physicallyBasedShading = true also gives invalid, noisy output.

OK. That is what I expected. I can't test this because I do not have the hardware.
Please set `specular` to zero in r.65. If the problem goes away, it is the specular component.

EDIT - no, that is not necessarily right... Below is the relevant code from `ShaderChunk.js`. Could it be the `pow` function that is causing the problem?

```
// specular

"vec3 pointHalfVector = normalize( lVector + viewPosition );",
"float pointDotNormalHalf = max( dot( normal, pointHalfVector ), 0.0 );",
"float pointSpecularWeight = specularStrength * max( pow( pointDotNormalHalf, shininess ), 0.0 );",

// 2.0 => 2.0001 is hack to work around ANGLE bug

"float specularNormalization = ( shininess + 2.0001 ) / 8.0;",

"vec3 schlick = specular + vec3( 1.0 - specular ) * pow( 1.0 - dot( lVector, pointHalfVector ), 5.0 );",
"pointSpecular += schlick * pointLightColor[ i ] * pointSpecularWeight * pointDiffuseWeight * lDistance * specularNormalization;",
```

Right, specular is most likely not causing this. I think it was already 0 (not set explicitly), but setting it explicitly to 0 does not change anything, the output is still invalid: http://jsfiddle.net/Z6CVP/3/

Hack the definition of `schlick` like so, recomplie, and see if the problem goes away.

```
"vec3 schlick = specular;",
```

Try setting `specular` to `0x111111` and `0x555555` and `0xffffff`.
Done, the problem goes away for all three values of specular.

OK, then the `pow` function _does_ seem suspicious. One more test,  please. Change the `5` to a `4`. That way, the result should always be positive.

```
"vec3 schlick = specular + vec3( 1.0 - specular ) * pow( 1.0 - dot( lVector, pointHalfVector ), 4.0 );",
```

Changing 5 to 4 does not help. Wrapping `pow()` in `max()`, the way it is done in some other places helps:

```
"vec3 schlick = specular + vec3( 1.0 - specular ) * max(pow( 1.0 - dot( lVector, pointHalfVector ), 5.0 ), 0.0 );",
```
And changing `5` to `3` helps.

OK, then the `pow` function appears to be generating garbage on your machine.

Thank you, @wrr,  for your clever detective work. :-)
@WestLangley I was only doing a job of a remote terminal ;)
@wrr Well, then, +1 for using `git bisect`. :-)

I can send a pull request with a fix, but what would be a proper approach?

My understanding of the problem is that `dot( lVector, pointHalfVector)` can yield a value that is larger than `1.0` (`1.0 + very small delta` maybe), which makes the base of the power negative. According to [GLSL spec](http://www.khronos.org/registry/gles/specs/2.0/GLSL_ES_Specification_1.0.17.pdf)(section 8.2), result of the `pow()` function with a negative base is undefined.

There are two possible reasons why the problem manifests itself only with some drivers:
1. Some drivers may handle `pow()` with negative base, even though it is not required by the standard.
2. Or the result of `dot( lVector, pointHalfVector)` may be always `<= 1.0` with drivers that yield good looking results.

Is this a correct understanding?

If so, maybe a valid fix would be:

```
 "vec3 schlick = specular + vec3( 1.0 - specular ) * pow( max( 1.0 - dot( lVector, pointHalfVector ), 0.0 ), 5.0 );",
```

Such code ensures that a base of the power is not smaller than `0.0`, so always yields a well defined result (unless `0.0` constant can be handled on some hardware as `0.0 - very small delta`, I'm not sure if this can be the case).

Actually, `dot(  lVector, pointHalfVector )` should never be greater than `1.0`, and in your example, it should be exactly `1.0` across the face of the cube. So what is happening is due to floating-point errors. On your machine the value varies around `1.0 +/- epsilon`.

Your suggested PR is fine, but it needs to be done everywhere. Here are some instances, but there are others in different files.

```
"vec3 schlick =       specular + vec3( 1.0 - specular ) * pow( 1.0 - dot( lVector, pointHalfVector ), 5.0 );",
"vec3 schlick =       specular + vec3( 1.0 - specular ) * pow( 1.0 - dot( lVector, spotHalfVector ), 5.0 );",
"vec3 schlick =       specular + vec3( 1.0 - specular ) * pow( 1.0 - dot( dirVector, dirHalfVector ), 5.0 );",
"vec3 schlickSky =    specular + vec3( 1.0 - specular ) * pow( 1.0 - dot( lVector, hemiHalfVectorSky ), 5.0 );",
"vec3 schlickGround = specular + vec3( 1.0 - specular ) * pow( 1.0 - dot( lVectorGround, hemiHalfVectorGround ), 5.0 );",
```
